newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet amends 1997 budget after tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet amends 1997 budget after tax cut.

text.p: The Polish government on Wednesday approved amendments to its 1997 budget draft by increasing the deficit to take account of a tax cut recently approved by parliament, a deputy finance minister said.

Halina Wasilewska-Trenkner told a news conference the amendment increases the deficit by 0.9 billion zlotys to 12.2 billion zlotys, or 2.8 percent of gross domestic product. The gap was originally planned at 2.6 percent of GDP.
Wasilewska-Trenkner said the higher deficit would be financed mainly by increasing the value of bond issues on foreign markets by $200 million to a total of $500 million.
"We set the maximum limit on the value of these bonds at $500 million," she said.
She said part of the deficit would be financed by different instruments but declined to give details.
The amendment to the draft, now discussed by parliament, sets revenues at 115.1 billion zlotys, down from an earlier planned 116.4 billion.
Spending was lowered to 127.3 billion from 127.7 billion by reducing the central government's budgetary reserve.
Parliament's decision earlier this month to cut income tax levels reduced projected 1997 tax revenue by about 2.5 billion zlotys.
But Wasilewska-Trenkner said the fall would be partly offset by higher revenues from value added and excise taxes and customs duties.
She confirmned the amended budget draft envisaged higher revenues from the privatisation of banks, rising by 950 million zlotys to 1.45 billion zlotys.
Analysts say this means the government would have to privatise large Bank Handlowy SA in 1997 and not only Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA as originally planned.
Wasilewska-Trenkner said the finance ministry thought the revenues from the banking privatisation could be much higher but declined to give details.
